message.content:
Let  
\[
x=\tan b>0.
\]
Since \(\tan a=5\tan b\), we have
\[
\tan a=5x.
\]

Because \(a,b\) are acute and \(5>1\), we get \(a>b\), so \(\sin(a-b)>0\). Now
\[
\tan(a-b)=\frac{\tan a-\tan b}{1+\tan a\tan b}
=\frac{5x-x}{1+5x^2}
=\frac{4x}{1+5x^2}.
\]
Let \(T=\tan(a-b)\). Since \(a-b\in(0,\pi/2)\),
\[
\sin(a-b)=\frac{T}{\sqrt{1+T^2}},
\]
which is increasing in \(T>0\). So we maximize
\[
T=\frac{4x}{1+5x^2}.
\]
Using AM-GM or differentiation, \(T\) is maximized when
\[
1=5x^2 \implies x=\frac1{\sqrt5}.
\]
Then
\[
T_{\max}=\frac{4/\sqrt5}{1+5(1/5)}
=\frac{4/\sqrt5}{2}
=\frac{2}{\sqrt5}.
\]
Thus
\[
\sin(a-b)_{\max}
=\frac{2/\sqrt5}{\sqrt{1+4/5}}
=\frac{2/\sqrt5}{3/\sqrt5}
=\frac23.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac23}\).
